full_judgment:
12. In course of hearing Mr Khandaker Mahbub Hossain, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the convict-appellant Abdus Salam @ Moti in Criminal Appeal No. 6143 of 2009 namely convict A. Salam Moti here shortly as Moti and submits that though the convict Moti was convicted for murder of constructive liability along with the other convicts but the prosecution has failed to prove the ingredients of section 141 of the Penal Code as well as also failed to prove the collective or vicarious liability of the accused-appellant thereby the conviction and sentence under sections 302/149 of the Penal Code against the accused appellant Moti is liable to be set aside. He further submits that as per the prosecution case the PW 3 namely Md Nadim was injured by the accused-appellant but the prosecution failed to prove the fact that the convict was a member of said unlawful assembly of the offence and, as such, the accused-appellant is liable for commission of individual liability for committing injury upon PW 3 therefore the conviction and sentence under section 302 read with section 149 of the Penal Code cannot be sustained in the eye of law. He further submits that the accused-appellant was absconded not for his fault however the said absconsion of the convict can not the basis of conviction but the trial Court mere on the basis of the fact of said absconsion along with the submission of the Public Prosecutor (PP) found guilty of the accused-appellant due to his absconsion from the trial which is bad in law as well as against the provision of section 8 of the Evidence Act, therefore, the conviction and sentence is liable to be set aside. He also submits that according to deposition of P W 3 who was injured on the right leg by the accused-appellant and no one has come forward to depose that the victim, PW 3 is a man of the informant. So the common object for the prosecution in respect of the accused-appellant was not proved beyond reasonable doubt and thereby the impugned judgment and order is liable to be set aside. He after drawing our attention in the statements of inquest report of the dead bodies of the victims and submits that the statements of inquest reports is also a primary evidence which can be considered to contradict or to corroborate of the prosecution case but in the present case the statement of the inquest report are not corroborated with prosecution case thus the prosecution case has become doubtful, therefore, the accused-appellant is entitled to get the benefit of doubt. 

 "Offence committed in prosecution of common object-section 149 Penal Code by itself creates no offence. It carries the liability of each member of an unlawful assembly for the act done in prosecution of their common object." 

 "Expression in prosecution of the common object explained-Ingredients that must be established to bring the charge home u/s 149." 

 (1) The accused must be a member of an unlawful assembly when the offence was committed, (ii) the offence must have been committed in prosecution of the common object of that assembly or (iii) the offence must be such as the members of the assembly knew it likely to be committed in prosecution of their common object. 

 When it is found that particular offence has been committed by an individual member of the unlawful assembly, which was neither done in prosecution of the common object of the assembly not other members of the assembly, knew that such an offence would be committed, other members of the unlawful assembly cannot be held liable for that offence." 

 "The mere fact that the accused were identified in a crowd and were arrested from the house where the occurrence had taken place is not sufficient is establish that they also shared the common object of the unlawful assembly. It may well be that they were silent spectators who out of fright took shelter with others there. In the circumstances they should be given the benefit of doubt and acquitted. 

 Section consist of two parties with respect the common object all may be found guilty but those who individually commit a lesser offence, they may individually he convicted of such offence under the 2nd part of section 149." 

 "The section creates a distinct and separate offence in the sense it imposes vicarious or constructive criminal liability of the members of an unlawful assembly for any offence committed by any member of such assembly in prosecution of the common object." 

 "When a particular offence is committed by an individual member of the unlawful assembly, which was neither done in prosecution of a common object of the assembly nor other members of the assembly knew that the offence would be committed, other members of the assembly cannot be held liable for the offence." 

 "Member of an unlawful assembly-Whether he can be convicted when the principal offender has not been convicted-Once the court finds that an offence has been committed by any member of an unlawful assembly in prosecution of its common object, then whether the principal offender has been convicted or not all other member may be constructively liable for conviction." 

 "Mere membership of an unlawful assembly makes one liable u/s. 149; u/s. 34 there is participation in an act with common intention. The basis of constructive guilt under section 149 is mere membership of an unlawful assembly; the basis of the offence under section 34 in participation in an act with common intention of doing that act. So, where common intention and common object are the one and same is a given case, both these sections may apply." 

 "For applying section 149 against an accused whether there conditions must be fulfilled before applying section 149 whether the Court must have indubitable evidence about member of the unlawful assembly. (i) For applying section 149 against an accused three conditions must be fulfilled; (a) The accused must have been a member of the unlawful assembly at the time the offence was committed; (b) the offence must have been committed in prosecution of the common object; (c) the offence must be such as the members of the assembly knew to be likely to be committed the prosecution of that object." 

 "In order to find a person or persons guilty of offence under section 302 read with section 149 of the Penal Code prosecution must establish that the offence was committed by any member of common object of the assembly or such as the members of that assembly knew that an offence would be committed in a prosecution of common object. Mere presence at the scene does not make a member of unlawful assembly liable for the offence unless it is proved that he shared common object of unlawful assembly. In the present case the prosecution totally failed to prove the charge under sections 302/149 of the Penal Code against the condemned prisoners and appellants." 

 "Section-302/ 149 "For finding the accused persons guilty under sections 302/149 of the Penal Code it is essential that the prosecution must prove and the court must found that the members of the unlawful assembly shared the common object of killing the victim. In the absence of a clear common object for murder, conviction under sections 302/149 of the Penal Code is not maintainable in law." 

 "The section creates a distinct and separate offence is the sense it imposes vicarious or constructive criminal liability of the members of an unlawful assembly for any offence committed by any member of such assembly in prosecution of the common object." 

 "Common object of unlawful assembly-The Additional Sessions Judge did not give any finding and the unlawful assembly had any common object of committing any particular offence—In the absence of any proof or any finding of any common object none of the accused could be found guilty. Penal Code (Act XLV of 1860) section 148." 

 33. In the case of Bhudeo Mandal vs State, reported in 1981 CRiLJ 725 (Supreme Court) wherein their lordship's held that; "Conviction under section 326 with the aid of section 149-Clear finding as to common object of assembly the pre-condition." 

 "It is now settled law that whenever a Court convicts any person for an offence with the aid of. Section 149. IPC a clear finding regarding a common object of the unlawful assembly must be given and the evidence discussed must show not only the nature at the common object but also that the object was unlawful. Before awarding a conviction under section 149, IPC the essential ingredients of the same provision of law must be established. Section 149, IPC creates specific of fence and deals with the punishment of that offence. There must be a common object." 

 (B) Penal Code (45 of 1860). Section 149 -Unlawful assembly and common object-Words "in prosecution of common object" occurring in section 149-Have to be strictly construed to mean "in order to attain the common object"-Word "object" means purpose or design and in order to make it "common" it must be shared by all-Proof of overt act-Not necessary." 

 "Penal Code (1860). Sections 147, 148 and 149—No evidence as to formation of unlawful assembly with common object-Sudden fight on spar of moment-Accused cannot be convicted under sections 147, 148 or 149. Decision of Madras High Court, Reversed." 

 42. Mr Khurshid Alam Khan, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the accused-appellants Munna and three others in Criminal Appeal No. 3485 of 2008 and submits that in a case of vicarious liability, the law provides that the offence must be committed in prosecution of the common object of the assembly or the offence committed must be such as the members of the assembly knew it likely to be so committed. The word "knew" imports a sense of expectation founded upon the facts that an offence of a very particular kind would be committed in prosecution of that common object of the assembly, which is something more than mere speculation. Further, acts committed in prosecution of the common object must also be proved by some over acts committed by others to that effect and in the absence of proved individual over act the charge of acting jointly shall also fails. He further submits that the accused appellants Munna and 3 (three) others who have no over act and there is no any legal evidence in commission of any injury of the victim or they attempt to commit any injury upon the victim is available under the facts and circumstances of the present case therefore the charge under sections 302/149 of the Penal Code was not proved beyond reasonable doubt against the said accused-appellants and, as such, they are liable to be acquitted from the charge as leveled against them. He further submits that the sections 149 of the Penal Code by itself does not create any offence at all it create the liability of the member of unlawful assembly for the act done to the prosecution in common object of unlawful assembly but the present appellants do not come with in the ambit of requirement of law under section 149 of the Penal Code therefore their conviction under section 302 read with 149 of the Penal Code cannot be sustained in the eye of law. He further submits that since there is no specific over act against the accused-appellants regarding the unlawful assembly as well as constitute the common object of the prosecution so, the question of knowledge about the common object of the accused-appellants do not arise at all. Even the said knowledge of common object of the prosecution which is required to be proved by the prosecution but the prosecution failed to prove the same even prosecution also failed to prove that the accused-appellants are the party men along with the convict A. Aziz and there is no over act for committing any injury upon any of the victims against the appellants and even no over act for attempt to murder of the victims is available in the materials on records. Therefore, the case of these appellants do not fall neither within the ambit of sections 302, 307 and 149 of the Penal Code and, as such, the impugned judgment and order in respect of his accused-appellants are liable to be set aside. 

 "In a case of vicarious liability, the law provides that the offence must be commit-ted in prosecution of the common object of the assembly or the offence committed must be such as the members of the assembly knew it likely to be so committed. The word "knew" imports a sense of expectation founded upon facts that an offence of a very particular kind would be committed in prosecution of that common object of the assembly, which is something more than mere speculation. Further, acts committed in prosecution of the common object must also be proved by some overt act committed by others to that effect and in the absence of proved individual overt act the charge of acting jointly shall also fail. To warrant a conviction vicariously by the application of section 149 there ingredients must be proved beyond all reasonable doubt and when they are wanting a person cannot be visited with the consequences of the offence and with the vengeance of the law vicariously by the application of section 149 of the Penal Code for a sudden violent act committed by a few (members of an unlawful assembly), traveling beyond the common object, all cannot be held guilty and convicted under sections 302/149 (when the common object of the assembly was dispossession of land)." 

 "B. Penal Code, 1860-Section 149-Applicability-Mandatory for court before convicting accused with aid of section 149 to give clear finding regarding nature of unlawful common object-In absence of such finding as also any overt act on part of accused, mere fact that they were armed not sufficient to prove common object-Moreover, in order to attract section 149, it must be shown that incriminating act was done to accomplish common object of unlawful assembly and it must be within knowledge of other members as one likely to be committed in prosecution of common object-Essential ingredients of section 141 also need to be established-In instant case, there was no material to show that all the accused shared the common object, the object itself not being proved and their participation in tit was not made out by credible evidence-Besides, no overt act was attributed to any other accused except A-1 towards murder of deceased-Hence, conviction under section 149 unsustainable." 

 59. On the other hand Dr Md Bashir Ullah, the learned Deputy Attorney-General appearing on behalf of the State who after drawing our attention to the FIR as well as the depositions of the witnesses, seizure list, inquest report and post mortem report including the relevant portion of the impugned judgment and then submits that the PW 1 immediately after occurrence lodged the FIR against the accused-appellants and others accused persons on the specific allegation that on 31-1-1994 at 10-00 AM the occurrence has been started under the leader-ship of accused-appellant A Aziz along with his supporters whose names have been mentioned specifically and who all carried the deadly weapon as Rifles, Pistol, Gun, Cerise, Bombs etc who came and attacked upon the neighbours of the informants within the Nababgonj Road by forming an unlawful assembly of the accused persons including the appellants who were firing bullets ferociously upon the informant and his man for which 7 (seven) persons were killed by the bullet under the hand of the appellants and 13 persons were injured for the acts of firing by the accused-appellants and other co-accused persons. These materials facts were well proved by adducing 31 prosecution witnesses. He further submits that out of 31 prosecution witnesses 7 witnesses were injured victims who categorically mentioned the names and over act of the accused-appellants and 15 witnesses are the eye-witnesses of the occurrence who also categorically mentioned the name and over act along with their activity by the fire arms for which 7 persons were brutally killed. These oral evidence of the prosecution witnesses also supported and corroborated by the inquest reports of the dead bodies of the victims as well as the post mortem report of the deceased namely Rafiqul Islam @ Shah Alam, Delwar, Gazi, Nazrul Islam, Abdul Aziz and Yunus conducted by doctor PW 24. He also submits that the accused-appellants had a prior conspiracy and a common object to kill the victim as being the supporters of the informant which well proved by the evidence of PWs 1-23 and 25 and all the convicts were jointly by way of formed an unlawful assembly made attacked upon the supporters of the informant victims and caused injuries for which 7 persons met to their death due to injury and 13 persons have been injured and weapons which have been used as Rifles, Pistol, and which are also proved by recovery of bullet from the injured persons along with their activities and conducts which are well connected them with the offence under sections 148/303/302 read with section 149 of the Penal Code and thereby the conviction and sentence thereunder by the learned trial Court is very much proper and legal. He also submits that the condemned-prisoners A Salam @ Moti, Jaheed Hossain @ Natka Babu and appellant Monir Patwary were absconding long about 15 years. Though these convicts are the residence of the said locality where in the occurrence took place. It was also submitted that instant case is very much sensational case where in 7 (seven) persons have been killed and 13 (thirteen) persons brutally injured of that locality which commonly known as 7 (seven) murder case. So, the plea of the said convicts that they had no prior knowledge of the case cannot be believable. Rather their long absconsion proved the result of their guilts. 

 61. As such the absconsion of these 3 (three) appellants are also very much consistence with the materials on records and law as provided under section 8 of the Evidence Act. He further submits the convicts A Halim Shaheen @ Alim and A Aziz against whom specific over act of allegation there that they committed injuries upon the victims Nazrul Islam and Gazi for which said victim Nazrul Islam and Gazi met their death. They also liable for committing injuries upon the victim PWs 2 and 3. He also submits that it was accused-appellant A Aziz who was the team leader of the party and under whose leadership and his active participate along with deadly weapon in the occurrence which took place and he also injured the victim Gazi and PW 14 with an intention to kill them. Then he submits that the convicts Munna, Kanu @ Kalliya, Delowar Hossain Anda and Amir Hossain Amira who were also active member of the unlawful assembly who attacked along with the deadly weapons in their hands with the other accused persons and who committed injuries upon the victim by way of firing of bullets and caused injuries upon 20 persons out of which 7 (seven) were died and that occurrence took place at the joint acts of all the accused persons by forming an unlawful assembly with a common object to kill the informant and his partymen, their conducts activities carried of fire of arms along with the other co-accused persons are connected the accused-appellant with the ambit of section 149 of the Penal Code. As such their conviction and sentence thereunder with the substantive sections 302/307/148 of the Penal Code is very much legal and proper. 

 62. He also after drawing our attention about the contention of the evidence including the cross-examination of the defence and submits that all the evidence including the victims who were injured and as being the eye-witnesses who saw the occurrence who narrated the occurrence about the time, place and manner including the over acts. The acts along with the arms, which were carried being the members of the unlawful assembly in course of occurrence. The evidence of such witnesses are also consistent with the facts of the prosecution and, as such, these evidences of those neutral and vital witnesses can not be discarded or disbelieved the testimony of the said eye-witnesses as well as the injured witnesses who injured at the hands of the accused-appellants. As such there is no reason to disbelieve that it was accused-appellant A Aziz under whose leadership the other convict appellants including A Aziz with deadly weapons by forming an unlawful assembly with a common object to kill the informant and his supporters attacked upon them on the date of occurrence on 31-1-1994 at 10-00 AM at Nababgonj Road and wherein the appellants and others mercilessly were firing upon the victims and committed injuries and for which 7 (seven) persons died and 13 (thirteen) persons were injured in the said incidents. As such their conviction and sentence by the impugned judgment and order are very much legal and proper. 

 "Common object-Inference of-Inferable from nature of weapons used, manner and sequence of attack and the setting and surroundings under which occurrence took place-Accused persons appearing at the scene of occurrence with lethal weapons in their hands and mercilessly assaulting the deceased after surrounding him-Held, clearly exhibits that their common object was nothing but to kill the deceased." 

 "B. Penal, Code, 1860-section 149-"Common object"-Evidence-Held, direct evidence generally not available in respect thereof-Hence, the same has to be gathered from the acts committed and result therefrom." 

 69. Their lordship's further observed; "Penal Code, 1860-sections 149 and 34 "Common object"-Meaning of-Distinguished from "common intention"-Words and phrases-"Common", "object", "common object", "common intention" 

 70. Their lordship's also observed that; "Penal Code, 1860-S. 149-The two parts of the provision, explained and distinguished-Expression "in prosecution of common object" and word "knew" used therein-Meaning of, also explained." 

 "The distinction between the common intention required by section 34 and the common object set out in section 149 lies just there. In a case under section 149 there need not be a prior meeting of minds. It is enough that each has the same object in view and that their number is five or more and that they act as an assembly to achieve that object." 

 "Commonness of purpose is an inference of fact which courts of fact would be entitled to make." 

 78. He was cross-examined by the defence and in his cross-examination he stated that his area is very congested area he has five brothers and his father is alive and four brothers are living in the house of Nababgonj lane. There are 15/20 shops of Holding No. 20 of Nababgonj lane to Nababgonj Bazar mosque at the relevant time 3/2 storied building were under construction of holding No. 24. He did not know the name of the land lord of said land. He described the holding numbers, which are situated at Nababgonj Road and Nababgonj lane beside the mosque and shops. He also stated that Baitus Salam Jamy Mosque and A Aziz lane are situated behind the holding No. 190 and 191. He further stated that Nababgonj Bazar is a middle class bazar and this bazar sat at 8-00 AM up to 9-00/9-30 PM. There are 5/6 hundred of peoples were used to came in the Bazar and he heard that Awlad was arrested. He denied the suggestion that 17 persons were arrested of his party men and he also denied the suggestion that they were released at his instance being his man. He denied the suggestion that the accused persons did not attack his house and the house of his supporters. He also denied the suggestion that the police officer went to his office and he also denied the suggestion that one Kamal has been taken from Provat Hotel and beaten by his man and he also denied the suggestion that he did not beat the brother of Kamal. He denied all the suggestions of the defence that on 31-1-1994 all the accused appellants along with 60/70 persons with deadly weapons attacked upon the informant's house and also upon the houses of his supporters of his area and thereby forming on unlawful assembly the FIR named accused persons and others for the purpose of their common object they used to blast bombs and also firing with their arms and as a result 7 persons dead and 13 were injured. He also denied the suggestion that no occurrence took place in the said time, place and manner as stated by the prosecution. 

 132. He was cross-examined by the defence in where he categorically stated that on 31-1-1994 at the initial stage he was deployed as the Investigating Officer and he got it after recording the case at 23-50 hours. He got the investigation at night 11.50 hours. He also stated that the 6 persons were arrested under section 54 of the Code of Criminal Procedure through a GD that GD No. 1531 dated 31-1-1994 under section 54 of the Code of Criminal Procedure. He was arrested from what place it has been written in GD and there is no mentioning time in forwarding and the time is not required to mention in the forwarding and at the time of preparation of seizure list the case was not started. He also stated that there is no require GD while some things is seized outside the common certificate. He denied the suggestion that he did not prepare the seizure list. He also stated that he did not say who is the owner of holding No. 20 of Nababgonj Road. He did not know personally the witness of the seizure list. He also denied the suggestion that he pre-pare the false seizure list. He also denied the suggestion that he did not conduct the investigation properly. He also denied the suggestion that he conduct the investigation illegally. 

 145. In his cross-examination he stated that he went to the SI Hanif as per the commoned certificate of their duty and that certificate has been deposited with Police Station. He also stated that he was carried the dead bodies from the Dhaka Medical College Hospital to Dhaka Medical College Hospital morgue and after handed over the dead bodies at the morgue to the doctor then he identified the same and he came back and it takes one and half hour time to handed over the said dead bodies and he did not say how many time was required to conduct the inquest of each dead body. 

 153. It appears from the record that the trial Court after considering the FIR, charge sheet and other materials-on-record framed the charge for the allegation of committing murder of the deceased namely Rafiqul Islam, Delwar Hossain, Gazi Hossain, Anwar Hossain Anu, Nazrul Islam, Hafiz and Yunus along with in furtherance of common object and the said occurrence has been committed on 31-1-1994 at 10-00/11-00 AM and it was took place within Nababgonj Road and the manner of commission of the offence has been described as with deadly weapons by firing bullets of rifle, revolver, pistol and blasting bomb and also with an allegation for committing rioting as well as also committing injury with an intention to commit murder to the victim Md Nadim, Abdus Salam, Mujibur Rahman, Md Yunus, Md Bachchu Miah, Md Somi Ullah, Nur Hossain and Raju Ahmed and the said victims were examined as PWs 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7 and 14 and the victim Nur Hossain was not examined by the prosecution and thereby charged framed against the convicts and others under sections 302/149, 148 of the Penal Code and 307 read with section 149 of the Penal Code respectively. 

 154. For the purpose, to prove the charge the prosecution examined as many as 31 wit-nesses out of which PW 1 is the informant, PWs 2-7 and 14 are the victims witnesses and PWs 8, 9, 10, 11, 13, 14, 15, 16, 18, 19, 20, 21, 22 and 23 are the eye-witnesses, of the occurrence PW 17 in whose presence the victim his son Nazrul Islam gave statement by mentioning the names of some accused persons who injured him before his death and PW 24, is the doctor who held post-mortem of the 7 (seven) deceaseds, PW 25 is the Investigating Officer who held the investigation in pursuance of the common certificate before lodgin'g the FIR, PW 26, is the police officer who held inquest of the victims and prepared the reports of the 6 (six) dead bodies of the deceaseds save and except deceased Md Yunus, PW 27, PW 28 and PW 31 are the formal witnesses, PW 28 doctor who issued death certificate for the 6 deceased save and except Md Yunus, PW 30, is the Investigating Officer who held investigation of the case and submitted charge sheet against the convicts and others under sections 302/307/148/149. 

 155. It is admitted that this is a very sensational case in where 7 persons have been killed and 8 persons were injured in pursuance of the common object of the accused persons by forming an unlawful assembly with deadly weapons each and also by committing riot by the accused persons and in where they also created panic by blasting bombs and also mercilessly firing of bullet upon the peoples of that area for which 7 persons were killed and 8 per-sons were injured by bullets on the date, time and place within the Nababgonj Road. In such circumstances we need to scrutinize the materials on record very carefully that is why we would like to evaluate the evidences regarding the individual over act in commission of the offence as alleged by the prosecution to connect the accused-appellants with the alleged charges. 

 162. It further appears from the contents of the FIR that the names of the convicts have been mentioned in the FIR along with their specific overtact in joint participation for a common cause to kill the informant and his sup-porters due to fail of the commissioners election of the convict A Aziz with the informant. It was further revealed from the FIR that the convicts and others accused persons out of which 19 (nineteen) have been mentioned in the FIR PW 1 also mentioned 70/80 persons along with the convicts and all the convicts carried deadly weapons namely Pistol, Kata Rifles, Ramdao, hand bombs and Ballistic Cocktail and by making an unlawful assembly by way of rioting mercilessly firing and blasting bombs and cocktails upon the informant and his supporters for which 18 (eighteen) persons were brutally injured out of which 6 (six) persons died on the same day of the occurrence. 

 183. It appears from the said evidence of PW 20, namely Year Mahamud cousin of deceased Gazi Hossain who was an accompanied with his cousin and out of them Gazi got bullet injury in his presence. He narrated the said fact and this materials fact as disclosed by PW 20 as eye-witness and why the evidence of PW 20 though being the cousin of deceased Gazi shall be disbelieved when Gazi was injured in his presence and when the said PW 20 had no enmity with the convicts. Moreover we do not find any such materials contradiction in his evidence PW 20 with the evidence of PW 30 though he was not injured by the bullet in the hand of the convicts. But he narrated how his brother who was accompanied with him has been killed by the joint act of convicts and in pursuance of their common object ultimately out of the convicts the fire which was made by co-convict Shaheen by his fire arms which hit on the chest of his brother namely Gazi and as a result Gazi died. It was not uncertain that bullet could hit on the chest of the PW 20. The evidence of PW 20 also supported by the PW 26 who conducted and prepared inquest report of the deceased Gazi and found the injury on the chest of the dead body of Gazi and also by Doctor PW 24 and in his deposition he stated that he proved the post-mortem of Gazi who found chest injury and from where he recovered the bullet from the dead body of Gazi which was marked as Exhibit VIII, PW 24 opined that victim dead due to said bullet injuries. 

 217. It further appears if the bullets hit on the vital parts of the body of the said 8 victims in that case they could die along with other 7 (seven) deceaseds. But luckily these 8 (eight) victims saved. It further appears from the records as well as the injury and recovery of bullets shows that the opinions which have been passed by the doctor and with the nature of injuries as also found by PW 26 in the inquest reports then we have come to the conclusion that the arms which have been issued by the convicts and others at the time of commission of the offence only for the purpose to fulfill their common object. In such circumstances it is also proved that the common object of the convicts were nothing but to kill the said victims and accordingly 7 (seven) victims died for their bullets injuries and 8 (eight) victims were injured by bullets who did not die but luckily alived. 

 "Section 141. Unlawful assembly—An Assembly of five or more persons is designated an "Unlawful assembly" if the common object of the persons composing that assembly is— 

 Section 141 of the Penal Code defines an unlawful assembly and in its 5 clauses are enumerated the elements required in order to make an assembly an unlawful assembly. The requisites are that their must be 5 or more persons and their common objects shall be one of the objects mentioned in the 5 clauses. Though there are exceptional not to fall an unlawful assembly but when the accused showed criminal force which could over wise and intimidate his adversary and this must be judges objectively. An assembly to defend a right may not be unlawful but when it is dangerous to lay down a general proposition that such assembly cannot be unlawful. This section would apply only where the common object of an unlawful assembly is unlawful and it is also necessary that all the members must share the common object. The common object must be an immediate one and not one to be carried out at some future time. 

 "Section 149. Every member of the unlawful assembly guilty of offence committed in prosecution of common object:- If an offence is committed by any member of an unlawful assembly in prosecution of the common object of that assembly , or such as the members of that assembly knew to be likely to be committed in prosecution of that object, every person who at the time of the committing of the offence, is a member of the same assembly is guilty of that offence." 

 230. Section 149 does not create any substantive offence but the same is declamatory of the vicarious liability of the members of unlawful assembly for acts done in prosecution of the common object of that assembly or for such an offence as members of unlawful assembly knew to be likely to be committed in prosecution of the object. For application of such section 149 it is necessary (a) that one be a member of unlawful assembly (b) that in prosecution of common object of that assembly an offence should be committed by a member of that unlawful assembly and (c) that the offence should be of such a nature that members of that assembly new the offence to be likely to be committed in prosecution of their common objects. 

 235. PW 14 categorically stated that convict Aziz and other 8 convicts and others with the arms in their hands being the members of riotes and convict Aziz shoot bullet upon him and for which the left side of his chest was injured and PW 20 also stated that convict Aziz, Shaheen along with the names of others convicts as being the notes and members of unlawful assembly and out of which convicts Shaheen caused injury upon the chest of his cousin Gazi by the fire arms and that Gazi was injured in his chest and immediately thereafter he died. The manner of occurrence and the weapons which have been used by the convicts including the numbers of members of the assembly, the further allegations of shooting against as many as 6 convicts including the acts of highest decree of rioting of the convicts in the journey of the commission of the occurrence and also by their henious and joint acts they have killed 7 persons and injured 8 persons in the same occurrence immediately after formation of unlawful assembly, by the convicts well proved that convicts being the members of an unlawful assembly which used above manner force of violence in prosecution of their common object to kill the victims Rafique and 14 others as mentioned above by that unlawful assembly. As such each and every member is guilty even one of them did not do any firing upon the victims. 

 "If an offence is committed by any member of an unlawful assembly which used force of violence in prosecution of the common object of that unlawful assembly, each and every member is guilty even one of them did not do any over act." 

 "It is true that the members of the unlawful assembly in the instant case might not have the common object of murdering Fatick Mia but it is clear from the evidence that they had the common object of committing an offence of any nature including murder to any one of the other party. This common object is clear from the other party. This common object is clear from the fact that all of the appellants rushed to the place of occurrence armed with different weapon including deadly weapon. So, we are of the view that though there is evidence that only four of the appellants actually caused injury to the victim, the other three being members of that unlawful assembly are equally liable. Moreover, there is evidence to show that these three caused injury to those who came to the place of occurrence to rescue the victim." 

 "Once the court finds that an offence has been committed by any member of an unlawful assembly in prosecution of its common object then whether the principal offender has been convicted or not all other members may be constructively liable for conviction." 

 A. "Penal Code 1860—sections 149 and 141—Constructive liability of members of an unlawful assembly—"Common object" as defined in section 141 existence of —Proof in respect of— Held is essential— Proof regarding overt act, held not necessary—Determination of "Common object"—Relevant considerations for restated—Explaining the manner of formation of "Common object" held it can develop at the spot no instant— once formed, it may be exists up to a particular stage where after it may get modified or may be abandoned—Effect of section 149 may be different on different members of the same assembly. 

 B. Penal Code 1860—sections 149—"Common object"—Evidence— held, direct evidence generally not avail-able in respect thereof— Hence, the same has to be gathered from the acts committed and result therefrom. 

 C. Penal Code 1860— sections 149 and 34 —"Common object"—Meaning of—Distinguished from "Common intention"—Words and phrase—"Common", "object", "Common object", "common intention" 

 D. Penal Code 1860—sections 149—The two parts of the provision, explained and distinguished— Expression" in prosecution of common object and word "knew" used therein—Meaning of, also explained." 

 241. Wherein it was held that; "The crucial question to determine is whether the assembly consisted of five or more persons and whether the said persons entertained one or more of the common objects, as specified in section 141. It cannot be laid down as a general proposition of law that unless an overt act is proved against a person, who is alleged to be a member unlawful assembly, it cannot be said that he is a member of an assembly. The only thing required is that he should have under stood that the assembly was unlawful and was likely to commit any of the acts, which fall within the purview of section 141. The word "object" means the purpose or design and in order to make it "common" it must be shared by all. In other words the object should be common to the persons, who compose the assembly, that is to say, they should all be aware of it and concur in it. A common object may be formed by express agreement after mutual consultation, but that is by no means necessary. It may be formed at any stage by all or a few members of the assembly and the other members may just join and adopt it." 

 242. The provision of the said sections 141, 149 along with the decisions as cited 4 Supreme Court Cases 205, 12 BLT (AD) 196, 44 DLR (AD) 233 is discussed and considered by us side by side. We also find under the facts and circumstances of the case and the evidence as discussed above to constitute the offence as believed the requirement in where ingredients of the said provisions of law and in pursuance of the facts and law the charge as framed by the trial court against the convicts and those materials ingredients along with evidences in pursuance of said charges are very much present to connect all the convicts who had deadly weapons came and formed an unlawful assembly within the meaning of section 149 read with section 141 of the Penal Code with a common object to kill the victims and out of which the convicts have been committed the offence on the date, time, place of occurrence and in such manner of occurrence by way of firing by their arms and also blasting bombs. Those used of arms and bombs are very much proved by the oral as well as the documentary evidence. That is to say the recover the bullets from the dead body of the 6 victims namely Rafiqul Islam and 5 others. Those bullets well proved materials as exhibits VI to X and also recovery of pleat of bullet from the place of occurrence other materials of used bombs. The injuries as bullet injuries upon the body of the victims including of the subsequent conduct of the convicts and their obstruction along with mercilessly firing by their arms upon the informant and his supporters for a long period of about 1 hour in the area of the informant residence at Nababgonj road. Consequently 7 (seven) injured persons died and 8 (eight) persons were injured but luckily those 8 victims are injured saved. This above acts and consequence for the acts of the convicts well proved that the offence which were committed by the convicts duly and well attacked within the provision of said sections as charged and convicted by the trial Court. 

 243. Though Mr Md Khurshid Alam Khan, the learned Advocate submits that there is no over act of firing the arms against his client convicts appellants Munna and 3(three) others as such the said Munna and 3 others are not the same footing along with other co-convicts therefore their conviction and sentence by the impugned judgment and order cannot be legal and proper. In this regard, we have considered the provision of section 141 as well as 149 of the Penal Code including the decision as cited above specially 12 BLT (AD) 196 and 44 DLR (AD) 233 which well satisfied that the causing or non causing any injuries upon any victim is not condition precedent to attract the provision of section 149 of the Penal Code if the other requirements of law are fulfilled by the prosecution then any members of such unlawful assembly are equally liable with the other convicts who made fire and caused injuries upon the victims along with its consequences of the victims from the result of their injuries. Since we find that prosecution well proved that all the convicts including the convict Munna and 3 others on the date, time and at the place of occurrence came with deadly weapons and by firing and by blasting bombs by forming an unlawful assembly with a common object and that common object has been reflected by their acts of firing mercilessly upon the supporters of the informant and causing injuries and out of which 7 (seven) injured persons died and 8 (eight) persons injured well proved the common object of the convicts were nothing but to kill the supporters of the informant and this materials fact well proved by the prosecution beyond reasonable doubt. We find there is evidence that 7 convicts actually caused injury to the victims. The other convicts being the members of that unlawful assembly are equally liable with the other convicts who caused injuries upon the victims. 

 244. Moreover, we find that there are evidence-on-records that all the convicts were firing by their arms and blasting bombs upon the victims mercilessly being the supporters of the informant. So, all the convicts also took parts actively in commission of the offence. Therefore, we also find that for the above reasons the prosecution well proved that all the convicts were the members of an unlawful assembly and their acts also well attracted within the provision of section 149 of the Penal Code and the relevant provisions of law as mentioned above and also in the light of the decisions as cited above reported in 12 BLT (AD) 196, 44 DLR (AD) 233 and (2004) 4 Supreme Court Cases 205. In such view of the matter we find that since all the convicts were being the members of unlawful assembly committed murder of 7 (seven) victims and injured 8 (eight) victims with an intention to kill in pursuance of their common object to kill the victims as the supporters of the informant on the date, time, place and manner of occurrence well proved by the prosecution that is the prosecution well proved the charges under sections 302/149; 307/149/148 of the Penal Code and those charges were proved by the legal evidences as adduced by the prosecution against all the convicts including convict A Aziz. The decisions as cited by the learned Advocate for the convicts-appellants are not applicable under the facts of the case.
